title: Any one or the one: the plural persons

sections.title: The object decides, again
sections.content: With a plural subject the choice is the same as with *én* and *te*. After *egy*, a number or a bare noun, use the plural endings you know: *kérünk, kértek, kérnek*. After *a / az*, *ezt* or *azt*, use the definite ones: *kérjük, kéritek, kérik*. Compare the two sets side by side.

sections.title: Any one → the one
rows: Mi kérünk tejet. → Mi kérjük a tejet.
We ask for milk. → We ask for the milk.
Ők vesznek almát. → Ők veszik az almát.
They buy an apple. → They buy the apple.
Ti főztök levest. → Ti főzitek a levest.
You all cook soup. → You all cook the soup.

sections.content: Choose by the object, not by the number of people. *Ők* is plural either way, but *Ők vesznek almát* (any apple) and *Ők veszik az almát* (that apple) are different sentences.
